facts.fact: ICT is the convergence of computing (IT) and communication technology, not just hardware.
Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 by MeitY.
Digital India rests on nine pillars; Green Energy Corridors is NOT one of them.
e-Kranti is the Digital India pillar for electronic delivery of services.
e-governance models: G2C (citizen), G2B (business), G2G (government), G2E (employee).
UMANG = single services app; DigiLocker = verified documents; e-Sign = Aadhaar e-signature; API Setu = interoperability.
India Stack is open-API digital public infrastructure for identity, payments and data.
The Account Aggregator enables consent-based sharing of financial data.
ONDC is an open network for digital commerce, not one company's app.
UPI is operated by NPCI and was launched in 2016.
Monthly UPI transactions crossed 16 billion in 2024-25.
Aarogya Setu, CoWIN, DigiLocker and DIKSHA are built on open-source digital platforms.
The DPDP Act, 2023 is India's first dedicated data-protection law.
The DPDP Rules were notified in 2025 (14 November 2025).
The Data Protection Board of India can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore.
DPDP roles: Data Principal (individual), Data Fiduciary, Significant Data Fiduciary.
A child's (under 18) data needs verifiable parental consent.
Puttaswamy (2017) declared privacy a fundamental right.
The IT Act 2000 is India's primary cyber law, amended in 2008.
Section 66A was struck down in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015).
Section 79 gives intermediaries safe harbour; 43A covers data-breach compensation; 69 covers interception.
CERT-In (MeitY, Sec 70B) is the national cyber-incident response agency.
CERT-In's 2022 directions require incidents to be reported within 6 hours.
NCIIPC protects Critical Information Infrastructure under NTRO via Section 70A.
Cyber Swachhta Kendra is CERT-In's botnet-cleaning centre.
The National Cyber Security Policy was adopted in 2013.
I4C functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
1930 is the national helpline for financial cyber fraud; CFCFRMS freezes stolen money.
Phishing tricks out credentials; ransomware encrypts and demands payment; DDoS floods servers; man-in-the-middle intercepts.
IndiaAI Mission (2024) has an outlay of about ₹10,372 crore.
IndiaAI pillars include compute capacity (GPUs), AIKosh datasets, FutureSkills and Safe & Trusted AI.
MeitY advisories under IT Rules 2021 address deepfakes and labelling of AI content.
Commercial 5G was launched in India in October 2022.
Bharat 6G Vision (2023) aims at 6G leadership by about 2030.
The National Quantum Mission (2023, about ₹6,003 crore) supports quantum-secure communication.
Semiconductor units: Dholera and Sanand (Gujarat), Jagiroad/Morigaon (Assam).
The India Semiconductor Mission has an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
PARAM Rudra supercomputers (National Supercomputing Mission, C-DAC) were dedicated in 2024.
BharatNet takes fibre broadband to gram panchayats; PM-WANI gives public Wi-Fi; CSCs deliver rural G2C services.
MeghRaj (GI Cloud) is the government's cloud-computing initiative.
AP's Real Time Governance Society runs a real-time monitoring centre.
e-Pragati is AP's enterprise-architecture platform.
The Praja Sadhikara Survey collected household socio-economic data in AP.
Mana Mitra delivers AP services via WhatsApp under RTGS — a G2C model.
AP FiberNet (APSFL) is the state undertaking for fibre broadband, internet and cable TV.
Amaravati Quantum Valley is India's first quantum-computing hub, with an IBM Quantum System Two (156-qubit Heron).
TCS and L&T are partners in the Amaravati Quantum Valley.
Google's 1 GW AI data-centre hub (with Adani and Airtel) is at Visakhapatnam.
AP's RTGS (Real Time Governance Society) is different from RBI's RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement).
Blockchain is a public ledger no single user controls, permissionless, not only for cryptocurrency.
NFTs are unique (non-fungible) blockchain tokens, not a medium of exchange; cryptocurrency is fungible.
Web 3.0 is a decentralised web where users own their data.
Cloud models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS — Outlook and Yahoo Mail are SaaS.
NFC is contactless (radio fields), works within about 4 cm and can use encryption.
Li-Fi uses visible light (375-780 nm) and is faster than Wi-Fi.
VoLTE carries voice over 4G LTE; Project Loon was balloon-based internet.
Present AI can diagnose disease, do text-to-speech and write songs, but cannot wirelessly transmit power.
RFID, NFC, WLAN and Bluetooth are short-range communication technologies.
The term qubit belongs to quantum computing.
ARPANET (1969): US defence network that grew into the internet.
World Wide Web: created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989.
IPv6: 128-bit internet addresses (IPv4 uses 32-bit).
DNS (Domain Name System): translates domain names into numeric IP addresses.
HTTPS: HTTP secured with encryption (TLS) — shown by the padlock in the browser.
Public internet in India: launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995.
Optical fibre: carries light signals by total internal reflection.
2G (GSM): first digital mobile generation — brought SMS.
4G LTE: all-IP mobile broadband; voice on it is VoLTE.
5G: very high speed, very low latency, supports massive IoT.
Telecommunications Act, 2023: replaced the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
TRAI (1997): Telecom Regulatory Authority of India — regulates tariffs and service quality.
Sanchar Saathi (DoT, 2023): portal and app to block lost phones (CEIR) and check mobile connections in your name.
Satellite broadband (GMPCS): internet from low-Earth-orbit satellites; spectrum assigned administratively under the 2023 Act.
Netiquette: the code of polite, responsible behaviour on the internet ("net etiquette").
Typing in ALL CAPITALS: reads as SHOUTING — avoid it.
Flaming: posting hostile, insulting messages.
Trolling: deliberately provoking others online to start fights.
Spamming: sending unwanted bulk messages.
Respect privacy and copyright: do not share others' personal data or copy content without credit.
Verify before forwarding: check facts to stop fake news and misinformation.
Virus: attaches to a host file and spreads when the file is run.
Worm: self-replicates across networks without a host file.
Trojan horse: malware disguised as useful software.
Spyware / keylogger: secretly records activity or keystrokes.
Rootkit: hides deep in the operating system to keep control.
Botnet: network of infected "zombie" computers run by an attacker, often used for DDoS.
Zero-day: a flaw exploited before the vendor has released a fix.
WannaCry (2017): worldwide ransomware attack on Windows computers.
Stuxnet (2010): worm that sabotaged Iran's uranium-enrichment centrifuges.
Cryptojacking: secretly using a victim's computer to mine cryptocurrency.
SQL injection: malicious code typed into a website form to read its database.
Spear phishing: phishing aimed at one specific person or organisation.
Whaling: phishing aimed at top executives.
Vishing: voice phishing over phone calls.
Smishing: phishing by SMS text messages.
Pharming: redirecting users from a real website to a fake one.
Quishing: phishing through malicious QR codes.
SIM-swap fraud: getting a duplicate SIM to receive the victim's OTPs.
Juice jacking: stealing data through infected public USB charging points.
"Digital arrest" scam: fraudsters pose as police or officials on video calls and extort money.
Deepfake: AI-generated fake video or voice of a real person.
Firewall: filters incoming and outgoing network traffic by rules.
Encryption: scrambles data so only the key-holder can read it.
Two-factor authentication (2FA): adds a second proof such as an OTP to the password.
VPN (Virtual Private Network): encrypted tunnel over the public internet.
Ethical (white-hat) hacking: authorised testing to find weaknesses.
Honeypot: decoy system that lures and studies attackers.
CAPTCHA: test that tells humans from bots.
Dark web: hidden part of the internet reached through special software such as Tor.
Section 43: damage to a computer system without permission — civil compensation.
Section 65: tampering with computer source code.
Section 66: computer-related offences such as hacking.
Section 66C: identity theft (misusing passwords, digital signatures).
Section 66D: cheating by personation using a computer.
Section 66E: violation of privacy — capturing or sharing private images.
Section 66F: cyber terrorism — punishable with up to life imprisonment.
Section 67 (67A, 67B): publishing obscene, sexually explicit or child sexual abuse material.
Section 69A: power of the Centre to block websites and online content.
Section 75: extra-territorial jurisdiction — offences abroad that involve a computer in India.
Commencement: the IT Act came into force on 17 October 2000.
Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA): licenses the bodies that issue digital signature certificates.
Cyber Appellate Tribunal: merged into TDSAT in 2017.
IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021: grievance officers for platforms; three-tier code for digital news and OTT.
Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025: bans real-money online games; promotes e-sports (assent 22 August 2025).
DPDP Act, 2023 — assent: received Presidential assent on 11 August 2023.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023: lists cyber-crime within "organised crime" (Section 111).
CERT-In: set up in 2004.
NCIIPC: notified in January 2014.
I4C: launched in January 2020 (approved 2018) under the MHA.
National Cyber Security Coordinator: heads cyber-security coordination in the National Security Council Secretariat (PMO).
Defence Cyber Agency: tri-service agency for military cyber operations.
National Informatics Centre (NIC, 1976): builds and hosts the government's websites and e-governance systems.
C-DAC (1988, Pune): built PARAM 8000 (1991), India's first supercomputer.
C-DOT (1984): telecom R&D centre founded under Sam Pitroda.
UIDAI (2009): issues the 12-digit Aadhaar number; statutory under the Aadhaar Act 2016.
Budapest Convention (2001): Council of Europe cybercrime treaty — India is not a party.
UN Convention against Cybercrime: adopted December 2024; opened for signature in Hanoi, October 2025.
NeGP (2006): National e-Governance Plan of Mission Mode Projects.
2nd ARC — SMART governance: Simple, Moral, Accountable, Responsive, Transparent.
JAM trinity: Jan Dhan accounts + Aadhaar + Mobile — the base for Direct Benefit Transfer.
BHIM (2016): NPCI's UPI app.
e-RUPI (2021): purpose-specific prepaid digital voucher on UPI.
Digital rupee (e₹): RBI's central bank digital currency — retail pilot since December 2022.
GeM (2016): Government e-Marketplace for public procurement.
e-NAM (2016): online national market for farm produce linking mandis.
Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (2021): 14-digit ABHA health ID and digital health records.
eSanjeevani: national telemedicine service.
SWAYAM (2017): free online courses (MOOCs).
DIKSHA (2017): digital learning platform for school teachers and students.
MyGov (2014): citizen-participation platform for ideas and feedback.
PRAGATI (2015): the Prime Minister's video-conference platform to review projects and grievances.
CPGRAMS: online public-grievance redress system of the Centre.
Bhashini (2022): AI platform for translation across Indian languages.
e-Courts Mission Mode Project: digitises court records and allows e-filing and virtual hearings.
UPI abroad: accepted in Singapore, the UAE, France, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Mauritius.
UPI volume (August 2025): about 20 billion transactions in a single month.
John McCarthy: coined "artificial intelligence" at the Dartmouth conference, 1956.
Turing test (1950): Alan Turing's test of whether a machine's replies can pass for a human's.
Machine learning: computers learn patterns from data instead of fixed rules.
Deep learning: machine learning with many-layered neural networks.
Large language model (LLM): generative AI trained on huge text to produce human-like language (e.g. ChatGPT).
Artificial general intelligence (AGI): hypothetical AI matching humans across all tasks (today's AI is narrow).
Internet of Things (IoT): everyday devices with sensors connected to the internet — term coined by Kevin Ashton (1999).
Edge computing: processing data near its source instead of a distant cloud.
Big data: data sets defined by volume, velocity and variety.
Digital twin: live virtual copy of a physical object or system.
AR vs VR: augmented reality overlays digital objects on the real world; virtual reality replaces it entirely.
3D printing: additive manufacturing — building an object layer by layer.
Superposition: a qubit can be 0 and 1 at the same time.
Entanglement: linked qubits share one state even when far apart.
Quantum supremacy (2019): Google's Sycamore processor claimed a task no classical computer could do in practical time.
Quantum key distribution (QKD): sharing encryption keys whose secrecy is guaranteed by physics.
Moore's law: transistors on a chip roughly double every two years.
Vikram 3201 (September 2025): India's first fully indigenous 32-bit space-grade microprocessor — ISRO and SCL Mohali.
Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL): government chip fab at Mohali, Punjab.
Micron (Sanand, Gujarat): US firm's chip assembly and test (ATMP) unit.
Tata–PSMC (Dholera, Gujarat): India's first commercial semiconductor fab, with Taiwan's PSMC.
India Semiconductor Mission: launched December 2021 under MeitY.
AIRAWAT: India's AI supercomputer at C-DAC Pune.
Pratyush and Mihir; Arka and Arunika: weather-and-climate supercomputers at IITM Pune and NCMRWF Noida.
BharatGen (2024): government-funded multilingual, multimodal Indian AI model initiative.
India AI Impact Summit (February 2026): held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi — first in the series hosted by a Global South country.
Drone Rules 2021: liberalised drone flying with green, yellow and red airspace zones.
Amaravati Quantum Valley MoU (4 May 2025): AP signed with IBM, TCS and L&T to install a 156-qubit IBM Quantum System Two.
